mission: CHT studies the incentives that drive powerful technologies and argues that the same 'race for engagement' that harmed society through social media is now driving AI. It raises public awareness (the podcast Your Undivided Attention, The AI Dilemma talk, The Social Dilemma film), pushes policy that rewards better design, and helps people and communities regain agency.

key_work.title: The A.I. Dilemma
key_work.plain_summary: A widely viewed talk by Tristan Harris and Aza Raskin arguing that racing to deploy AI repeats social media's mistakes at far higher stakes, and that institutions must catch up.

key_work.title: Your Undivided Attention (podcast)
key_work.plain_summary: CHT's long-running podcast interviewing researchers, insiders and whistleblowers about technology, AI and society.

status_note: began with social media harms ('Time Well Spent', The Social Dilemma); expanded its focus to AI in the 2020s
status_raw: active — began with social media harms ('Time Well Spent', The Social Dilemma); expanded its focus to AI in the 2020s

warnings.text: AI is being shaped by the same race-for-attention and market-dominance incentives that harmed society through social media.
A small number of AI companies are racing to build extremely powerful systems faster than society can adapt.
AI can erode focus, relationships, mental health and democratic institutions, and could slip out of human control.
Engagement-optimised AI companions pose particular risks to young people.

recommendations.text: Change the incentives driving AI through policy (e.g. liability and design standards).
Pursue international coordination and treaties on AI.
Raise public understanding so citizens demand a different path.
Design technology to strengthen, not exploit, human attention and relationships.
